cases.title: A · Historical repayment patterns
cases.question: How do repayment-status categories relate to next-month default?
cases.method: Full-data descriptive rates with Wilson intervals, no causal inference.
cases.result: Observed prevalence 22.12%; 6,636 events among 30,000 released records.
cases.interpretation: Repayment status is a predictive association to investigate, not a causal lever.
cases.limitation: Historical Taiwan 2005 sample; undocumented codes retained.

cases.title: B · Logistic versus boosting
cases.question: Does nonlinear modeling improve probability quality?
cases.method: Three-fold training CV; separate validation; untouched final-test descriptive audit.
cases.result: Selected boosting by validation log loss. Final raw L2 log loss 0.4381; boosting 0.4292.
cases.interpretation: Discrimination and probability quality both matter; final comparisons do not select the model.
cases.limitation: One frozen random split; no out-of-time evidence.

cases.title: C · Discrimination and calibration
cases.question: Does independent calibration improve estimated probabilities?
cases.method: Calibration half-fit/half-selection; chosen method refit full calibration only.
cases.result: Chosen none. Final log loss 0.4292, Brier 0.1350, calibration slope 0.984.
cases.interpretation: Calibration changes probability scale; improved AUC alone does not imply accurate probabilities.
cases.limitation: Selection partition uncertainty and calibration estimates do not certify transportability.

cases.title: D · Illustrative loss sensitivity
cases.question: How do assumed shocks affect modeled loss?
cases.method: Odds stress times hypothetical LGD times hypothetical EAD times 1,000 accounts.
cases.result: Baseline modeled loss 9,936,454 NTD; severe assumed scenario 19,592,343 NTD.
cases.interpretation: Loss assumptions materially affect a scenario arithmetic result.
cases.limitation: No observed LGD/EAD, no IFRS9 or regulatory loss calculation.
